key_insight: PPO-based pit-stop planning modestly outperformed mathematical optimization under race uncertainty and enabled action-by-action forecasts of finishing outcomes.
engineering_relevance: Combining reinforcement learning with a calibrated simulator can support sequential operational decisions where uncertainty and competitors limit deterministic optimization.
method: Calibrate a race simulator with historical data, including tire wear, overtaking, yellow flags, and rival pit stops.
Compare five deep reinforcement learning algorithms against a quadratic mixed-integer programming baseline.
Use trained PPO for look-ahead comparisons of outcome distributions under candidate pit-stop actions.
evidence_signal: Across eight circuits, PPO averaged 0.33 positions better than QMIP in simulated races and 0.49 in 2024 race replays; in replays, it also beat simulated actual driver strategies by 0.66 positions.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based and retrospective; real-time deployment would require validation of simulator fidelity and robustness to unseen race conditions.
paper_title: AI-Assisted Decision Support for Formula 1 Pit-Stop Strategy: Deep Reinforcement Learning and Mathematical Programming
